sections.abstract: Vip3Aa, Vip3Ad, Vip3Ae, and Vip3Af proteins from Bacillus thuringiensis were tested for their toxicity 27 against Spodoptera frugiperda and Agrotis ipsilon. Vip3Ad was non-toxic to the two species. Vip3Ae and 28 Vip3Af were significantly more toxic than Vip3Aa against S. frugiperda, both as protoxins and as toxins. 29 Against A. ipsilon, Vip3Ae protoxin was more toxic than Vip3Aa and Vip3Af protoxins. Purification by 30 metal-chelate affinity chromatography significantly affected Vip3Ae toxicity against the two insect 31 species. 32 ## 36 Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) is a soil bacteri Q2 um with wide insecti-37 cidal activity against numerous species from different insect orders 38 (Schnepf et al., 1998). So far, Cry proteins are the most well-known 113 Laboratory colonies of S. frugiperda and A. ipsilon were reared on 114 artificial diet and maintained at 25 ± 3 °C with 70 ± 5% RH and a 115 16/8 h (light/dark) photoperiod. Surface contamination assays were 116 carried out by applying 50 ll of the sample dilutions on artificial diet 117 (in 2 cm 2 multiwell plates) and letting dry. Bioassays were repli-118 cated 3 or 4 times using seven concentrations of Vip3A protein sam-119 ples and 16 neonate larvae for each concentration. E. coli WK6 crude 120 extract (without Vip3A expression) was used as a negative control 121 when crude extracts of Vip3A-expressing clones were tested. Trays 122 were incubated at 25 °C and mortality was scored at 7 days. Regres-123 sion curves were estimated using the POLO-PC probit analysis pro-124 gram (LeOra Software, Berkeley, CA). LC 50 values were considered 125 significantly different when fiducial limits did not overlap. 126 Single dose bioassays using crude extract supernatants of the 127 E. coli cultures expressing Vip3Ae and Vip3Af were found very ac-128 tive against both insect species, whereas Vip3Ad had no activity 129 (4000 ng/cm 2 of this protein caused no mortality nor growth inhi-130 bition) (Table 1). To check whether the lack of toxicity of this pro-131 tein could be due to inefficient activation of the protoxins in vivo, 132 the crude extract was treated with trypsin and tested in bioassays. 133 Again, no activity was found for the trypsin-treated Vip3Ad protein 134 (Table 1). 135 Quantitative toxicity assays were carried out with Vip3Ae and 136 Vip3Af, either as protoxins or as activated toxins, and their activ-137 ity was compared to that of Vip3Aa (Table 1). For A. ipsilon, Vi-138 p3Ae protoxin in the crude extract was significantly more active 139 than Vip3Aa (3-to 4-fold) and Vip3Af (4-to 5-fold), whereas no 140 significant difference was found between Vip3Af and Vip3Aa. No 141 significant differences in activity were found among the trypsin 142 activated forms of Vip3Ae and Vip3Af. Metal-chelate affinity chro-143 matography purification resulted in a significant loss of activity of 144 Vip3Ae (20-fold as protoxin and 4-to 5-fold as activated toxin, 145 regarding the non-purified equivalent), whereas Vip3Af was not 146 affected. 147 Bioassays with S. frugiperda showed that Vip3Ae and Vip3Af in 148 crude extracts (either as protoxins or activated toxins) were signif-149 icantly more active than Vip3Aa (10-to 22-fold). No significant dif-150 ferences of activity between Vip3Ae and Vip3Af in crude extracts 151 were found either as protoxins or as activated toxins. Again, 152 Vip3Ae toxicity was significantly reduced after chromatography 153 purification (around 5-fold for both protoxin and toxin). Addition-154 ally, LC 50 values for Vip3Af were also increased after chromatogra-155 phy purification, although the differences were only significant for 156 the trypsin activated protein (6-fold). 157 Interestingly, in those cases where Vip3A proteins partially lost 158 activity after chromatography purification we observed a remark-159 able growth inhibition in the surviving larvae (data not shown). 160 Growth inhibition differences between purified and non-purified 161 proteins were not observed when mortality was not affected. To 162 determine the causes of the loss of activity of the Vip3Ae protein 163 during the purification by metal-chelate affinity chromatography, 164 the effect of imidazole and of Ni 2+ ions was tested. Vip3Ae crude 165 extract supernatants were incubated at 4 °C for 1 h, in 20 mM so-166 dium phosphate buffer, 0.5 M NaCl, pH 7.4, either with 100 mM 167 NiSO 4 or 150 mM imidazole. After incubation, samples were de-168 salted in Sephadex PD-10 columns (GE Healthcare) and eluted with 169 phosphate buffered saline (8 mM Na 2 HPO 4 , 2 mM KH 2 PO 4 , 170 150 mM NaCl, pH 7.4). Bioassays against S. frugiperda showed that 171 imidazole had no effect on the activity of the Vip3Ae protoxin 172 (LC 50 = 15 ng/cm 2 , FL 95 6-30) whereas Ni 2+ significantly reduced 173 its activity (LC 50 = 206 ng/cm 2 , FL 95 50-716).
